mainTopic: Windfall money and מצוות, sobering up from wine, and lessons from רבן גמליאל's journey
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list: when money comes easily, such as a husband's profit from נכסי אשתו, a big business gain, or a מציאה, a person should spend part of it on a מצוה like a ספר תורה or even תפילין, and a פסוק about Israel's vow is brought as a hint. The גמרא then turns to wine. רמי בר אבא says walking a מיל or a short sleep wears off wine, and רב נחמן limits this to someone who drank a רביעית. The גמרא challenges this with a ברייתא about רבן גמליאל, who had a man follow them three מילין before he would release the man's vow after drinking Italian wine. The ברייתא also teaches side lessons: רבן גמליאל's רוח הקודש, not passing by food, following the majority, a gentile's חמץ after פסח, and releasing vows only while sitting. The גמרא answers that Italian wine is stronger, and that riding is different from walking. It explains the need to sit for releasing vows as a dispute between תנאים about whether חרטה alone is enough. It then limits the rule about passing by food because of the fear of witchcraft: whole loaves may be passed by, but pieces may not. The amud ends by introducing a teaching of רב ששת in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last item on the list: a husband who gains from his wife's property
steps.stepSummary: The list of windfall cases ends with a בעל who gains rights to נכסי אשתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A husband who gains from his wife's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from the previous lines of cases where money comes easily. In these cases a person should use part of the money for a מצוה, like buying a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף the teaching was that 'easy money' tends not to last unless a person does a מצוה with some of it. This line adds a husband who gets the profits of property his wife brought into the marriage. He did not work for that money, so he should also set some aside for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife's property, which the husband may use and profit from
A Torah scroll, the מצוה purchase discussed in this list

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the end of a sentence that began on the previous amud, so read it as 'and also: a husband with his wife's property.'

phrases.english: A husband with his wife's property.
phrases.notes: Final case in the list of windfall money that should be partly used for a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who profits from his wife's property should use part of it for a מצוה so the rest will last.

steps.title: Adding more cases of easy money: business profit and a found object
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a big business profit. רב פפא adds a found object (מציאה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: even if he did a business deal and profited. רב פפא said: even if he found a lost object.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים make the list of windfall money longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says even money from a business deal counts if he made an unusually large profit, because it came beyond normal expectation. רב פפא goes further: a מציאה, which took no effort at all, also counts. Both widen the case. The rule itself stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, which signals that the case is being widened

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ עֲבַד עִיסְקָא וּרְוַוח.
phrases.english: Rava said: Even if he made a business deal and profited.
phrases.notes: He too should use part of the profit for a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מָצָא מְצִיאָה.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Even if he found a lost object.
phrases.notes: Another case of money that came easily.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the list of cases from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A large business profit and a found object also call for spending part of the money on a מצוה.

steps.title: Even writing תפילין with the money is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the מצוה does not have to be a ספר תורה. Writing תפילין also works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: even if he wrote תפילין with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא widens which מצוה can be done with the money, not which money counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 and 2 widened the kinds of money. Here רב נחמן בר יצחק widens the kind of מצוה. A ספר תורה is not required. Spending some of the money on תפילין also brings the merit that protects the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: With them, meaning with the money

steps.whatToRemember: With any windfall money, use part of it for a מצוה (a ספר תורה, or even תפילין) and the rest will last.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Even if he wrote phylacteries with it.
phrases.notes: A smaller מצוה than a Torah scroll is also enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֲפִילּוּ כְּתַב בְּהוּ תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from widening the cases of money to widening the kind of מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using the money to write תפילין is also enough.

steps.title: A verse hint: Israel's vow before battle
steps.stepSummary: רב חנין (or רבי חנינא) brings a פסוק as a hint: 'וידר ישראל נדר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנין said, and some say רבי חנינא: What is the verse for this? As it is written: 'And Israel vowed a vow' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that hints to the idea of setting aside part of one's gain for שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, Israel promised that if ה׳ gave them victory, they would dedicate the spoils of the cities to Him. This shows the pattern: when gain comes, dedicating part of it to Heaven brings blessing. It works as a hint for the practice in steps 1 to 3.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? A request for a scriptural source

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנִין, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥanin said, and some say Rabbi Ḥanina:
What is the verse? As it is written:
"And Israel vowed a vow," etc.
phrases.notes: במדבר כא:ב. The vow was to dedicate the cities' spoils to ה׳ if Israel won.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives scriptural support for the practice in steps 1 to 3.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of setting aside part of one's gain for a מצוה so that one succeeds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כא:ב, Israel's vow to dedicate the spoils to ה׳ in exchange for victory.

steps.title: Walking a מיל or a short sleep wears off wine
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא teaches that walking a מיל or sleeping even a little removes the effect of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: walking a מיל, and a sleep of any length, wear off the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier topic on this דף, drinking wine (for example, before תפילה or giving a ruling). It teaches how a person can sober up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the דף discussed someone who drank wine and is limited in certain things. רמי בר אבא gives two ways to remove that state: walking about a מיל, or sleeping for any amount of time. After either one, he counts as no longer under the wine's influence.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking a distance of a מיל, roughly 2000 אמות
Any amount at all, even minimal

phrases.english: Rami bar Abba said:
Walking a mil, and sleeping any amount at all —
dispel the wine.
phrases.notes: They remove its intoxicating effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא: דֶּרֶךְ מִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It returns to the דף's earlier discussion of wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walking a מיל or sleeping any amount wears off the effect of wine.

steps.title: This only works for someone who drank a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה limits רמי בר אבא's rule to someone who drank a רביעית. For more than that, walking and a short sleep make things worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: this was only taught about someone who drank a רביעית. But if he drank more than a רביעית, the walk tires him out all the more, and the sleep makes him more drunk.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא limits the rule from step 5 so it does not apply to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר אבא's rule is true only for a modest amount of wine, a רביעית. Someone who drank more is too affected. Walking just exhausts and confuses him, and a short nap leaves him drunker. The rule from step 5 stays, but now only within a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about, a formula that limits a rule
A quarter-לוג, a standard measure of liquid

steps.whatToRemember: Walking a מיל or a short sleep sobers someone who drank a רביעית. For someone who drank more, these make him worse.
steps.confusionAlert: 'כל שכן' here does not mean the rule applies even more strongly. It means the walking tires him all the more, so the rule does not help him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁתָה כְּדֵי רְבִיעִית,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he drank a quarter-log,
but if he drank more than a quarter-log —
all the more so the walk wears him out,
and the sleep makes him drunker.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁתָה כְּדֵי רְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from step 5 to someone who drank a רביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sobering effect of walking or sleeping applies only to someone who drank a רביעית. For more than that, they make him worse.

steps.title: Does walking a מיל really remove wine's effect? A story begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רמי בר אבא's rule that a מיל of walking removes wine's effect. It starts quoting a ברייתא about רבן גמליאל traveling from עכו to כזיב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can walking just a מיל really get rid of the effect of wine? But a ברייתא teaches a story: רבן גמליאל was riding a donkey from עכו to כזיב, and רבי אילעאי was walking behind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning רמי בר אבא's rule from Step 5 and starts telling a ברייתא story to prove its point. This step only sets the scene; the part of the story that actually challenges the rule comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר אבא said a short walk of one מיל takes away the effect of wine. Later in this ברייתא, רבן גמליאל drinks a רביעית of wine and has to travel three מילין before he is sober enough to release a vow (Step 14). That suggests one מיל is not enough. Right now the גמרא is only laying out who, where, and how they traveled.

keyTerms.meaning: From עכו to כזיב, a trip of several מילין

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the wine point here. The story about the loaves and the gentile seems unrelated, but the ברייתא keeps going. In Steps 13–14 we learn what happened with the wine at the end of the trip, and Step 16 is where the challenge lands.

phrases.english: And does a path of a mil dispel the wine?!
phrases.notes: A challenge to רמי בר אבא's rule in Step 5.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel
who was riding on the donkey
and was traveling from Akko to Keziv,
phrases.notes: Background for the story. The distance that matters for the challenge is the three מילין later on (Step 14).

phrases.english: and Rabbi Elai was walking behind him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of רמי בר אבא (Step 5), as limited by רב נחמן (Step 6), using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר אבא's rule that walking a מיל removes the effect of wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבן גמליאל needed three מילין of travel after drinking a רביעית before he could release a vow (Steps 13–14). So one מיל should not be enough.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל finds loaves and tells a gentile by name to take them
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells רבי אילעאי to pick up loaves from the road. Later he tells a gentile, calling him מבגאי, to take the loaves from אילעאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל found nice loaves of bread on the road. He said: אילעאי, pick up the loaves. Then he met a gentile and said: מבגאי, take these loaves from אילעאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא story continues. רבן גמליאל has the bread picked up and then hands it to a gentile, whom he calls by name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details matter later. First, he did not leave food lying on the road. Second, he gave the bread to a gentile instead of eating it. He also called the gentile by a name he should not have known, which the next step will explore.

phrases.english: He found fine loaves on the road,
he said to him: Elai,
take the loaves from the road.
He came across a certain gentile,
he said to him: Mavgai,
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל calls him by name, which is surprising.

phrases.english: take these loaves from Elai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא story that the challenge in Step 7 is built on.
steps.raayaObject: The background of the ברייתא used to challenge רמי בר אבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about רבן גמליאל on the road from עכו to כזיב.

steps.title: רבי אילעאי questions the gentile and learns רבן גמליאל never met him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעאי asks the gentile where he is from and what his name is. He also asks whether רבן גמליאל ever knew him. The answer is no.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעאי walked over to the gentile and asked: Where are you from? He said: From the guardsmen's towns. And what is your name? My name is מבגאי. Has רבן גמליאל ever met you? He said: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעאי checks how רבן גמליאל knew the gentile's name. He finds out the two had never met.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questions confirm that רבן גמליאל had no normal way to know the name מבגאי. This sets up the next line: he knew it through רוח הקודש. The detail that the man came from gentile towns also matters later for the rule about following the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: He joined him, went over to him

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai joined him,
he said to him: Where are you from?
He said to him: From the towns of guardsmen.
And what is your name?
Mavgai is my name.
Has Rabban Gamliel ever known you?
He said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explores the surprising detail from Step 8, that רבן גמליאל knew the gentile's name.
steps.raayaObject: Shows רבן גמליאל had no natural way to know the gentile's name.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about רבן גמליאל on the road from עכו to כזיב.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל knew the name through divine inspiration
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that רבן גמליאל guessed the name correctly through רוח הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment we learned that רבן גמליאל got the name right through רוח הקודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pauses the story to explain the mystery of the name. רבן גמליאל knew it through רוח הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבן גמליאל had never met the man, the only explanation is רוח הקודש. This line is a side lesson inside the story. It is not yet the point about wine.

phrases.english: At that time we learned
that Rabban Gamliel got it right through divine inspiration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבי אילעאי's questions in Step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן גמליאל knew the gentile's name through רוח הקודש.

steps.title: Three lessons from the story: first, do not pass by food
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says three הלכות were learned from the story. The first is that one may not pass by food lying on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned three things at that time. First: you may not walk past food lying on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts listing three practical הלכות learned from רבן גמליאל's actions. The first one comes from his having the bread picked up off the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל did not leave the loaves on the ground. He had רבי אילעאי pick them up, even though he did not plan to eat them. This teaches that food must be treated with respect, and you should not leave it lying where people pass.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not pass by food (and leave it lying there)

phrases.english: And we learned three things at that time:
We learned that one may not pass by food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the רוח הקודש lesson to practical הלכות drawn from the same story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not pass by food lying on the road. One must pick it up.

steps.title: Second and third lessons: follow the majority, and a gentile's חמץ after פסח
steps.stepSummary: The second lesson is that we follow the majority of travelers. The third is that a gentile's חמץ is permitted for benefit after פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned that we follow the majority of people traveling the road. And we learned that a gentile's חמץ is permitted for benefit after פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of three lessons from רבן גמליאל's actions with the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most travelers in that area were gentiles, so רבן גמליאל assumed the bread belonged to a gentile. That is why he did not eat it: following the majority. Because this happened just after פסח, giving the bread away was a kind of benefit (the gentile's gratitude). This shows that a gentile's חמץ that was kept over פסח may be used for benefit afterwards.

keyTerms.meaning: Travelers, people passing on the road
Leavened bread owned by a gentile

steps.whatToRemember: From one road incident, the ברייתא learns that רבן גמליאל had רוח הקודש, plus three הלכות: (1) don't pass by food, (2) follow the majority of travelers, (3) a gentile's חמץ is permitted for benefit after פסח. The wine challenge to רמי בר אבא is still coming, at the end of this trip.
steps.whyThisMatters: Each lesson is a lasting practical הלכה. The rule about a gentile's חמץ after פסח is especially important in הלכות פסח.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָמַדְנוּ שֶׁהוֹלְכִין אַחֲרֵי רוֹב עוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים.
phrases.english: And we learned that we follow the majority of travelers.
phrases.notes: Most travelers there were gentiles, so the bread was assumed to be a gentile's.

phrases.english: And we learned that leavened bread of a gentile
after Passover is permitted for benefit.
phrases.notes: Giving it away earned the gentile's goodwill, which counts as benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמַדְנוּ שֶׁהוֹלְכִין אַחֲרֵי רוֹב עוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three lessons begun in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We follow the majority of travelers to decide who owns lost food. A gentile's חמץ is permitted for benefit after פסח.

steps.title: A man asks to release his vow, and רבן גמליאל delays
steps.stepSummary: At כזיב a man asks רבן גמליאל to release his vow. רבן גמליאל confirms that they drank a רביעית of Italian wine, so he tells the man to follow them until the wine wears off.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבן גמליאל reached כזיב, a man came to ask about releasing his vow. רבן גמליאל asked the person with him: 'Didn't we drink a רביעית of Italian wine?' He answered: 'Yes.' רבן גמליאל said: 'If so, let him walk after us until our wine wears off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. רבן גמליאל refuses to handle a vow right away because he recently drank wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Releasing a vow is a halachic act, much like giving a ruling, and it needs a clear mind. רבן גמליאל checks with his companion that they really drank a רביעית of strong wine. Then he chooses to wait instead of acting while possibly affected. This part of the story is the source the גמרא will use to work out how long wine takes to wear off.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask a חכם to release (annul) one's vow
A quarter-לוג, the measure of wine that can make a person unfit to rule
Italian wine, known for being strong
Wears off, fades away (the effect of the wine)

phrases.english: When he arrived at Keziv,
a person came to ask about his vow (to have it released).
phrases.notes: A sage can release a person's vow if there is proper grounds.

phrases.english: He said to the one who was with him:
phrases.notes: The companion is רבי אילעאי.

phrases.english: Did we drink a quarter-log of Italian wine?
He said to him: Yes.
If so, let him travel after us
until our wine wears off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא story after the lessons about the loaves and the gentile.
steps.raayaObject: How long it takes for the effect of wine to wear off before one may perform halachic acts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about רבן גמליאל's journey from עכו to כזיב

steps.title: After three מילין, רבן גמליאל sits and releases the vow
steps.stepSummary: The man followed them for three מילין to סולמא דצור. There רבן גמליאל got off his donkey, wrapped himself, sat, and released the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The man followed after them for three מילין, until they reached סולמא דצור (the Ladder of Tyre). When they reached it, רבן גמליאל got off the donkey, wrapped himself in his garment, sat down, and released the man's vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Only after traveling three מילין does רבן גמליאל feel clear-headed enough to release the vow, and he does it in a formal, seated way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details matter here. First, the distance was three מילין, which is the number the גמרא will soon challenge. Second, רבן גמליאל did not release the vow while riding. He dismounted, wrapped himself like a judge, and sat, which shows the seriousness of the act.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural of מיל, a distance of roughly 1 km each
The Ladder of Tyre, a place on the coastal road north of עכו
He wrapped himself in his garment, as a judge does to sit with awe

phrases.english: And he traveled after them three mil,
until he arrived at the Ladder of Tyre.
When he arrived at the Ladder of Tyre,
Rabban Gamliel got down from the donkey,
and wrapped himself, and sat,
phrases.notes: Wrapping in a garment is the way of a judge sitting in judgment.

phrases.english: and released his vow for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the vow episode started in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The distance needed for wine to wear off (three מילין) and the proper posture for releasing vows

steps.title: Four lessons learned from the vow episode
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists four lessons: a רביעית of Italian wine intoxicates, a drunk person may not rule, traveling makes wine wear off, and vows may only be released while sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned many things at that time. We learned that a רביעית of Italian wine makes a person drunk. We learned that a drunk person may not give a halachic ruling. We learned that traveling on the road makes wine wear off. And we learned that vows may not be released while riding, walking, or standing, only while sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like the earlier list of three lessons (steps 11-12), the ברייתא now pulls practical rules out of the vow story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each lesson matches a detail in the story. Asking about the wine shows that a רביעית of Italian wine intoxicates. Waiting shows that a שיכור may not rule. The journey shows that travel sobers a person. Dismounting and sitting shows the required posture for releasing vows.

keyTerms.meaning: A drunk person may not give a halachic ruling
Annul vows (here used loosely for a חכם releasing a vow)

steps.whatToRemember: Four lessons: (1) a רביעית of Italian wine intoxicates, (2) a שיכור may not rule, (3) travel makes wine wear off, (4) vows are released only while sitting.
steps.confusionAlert: The word מפירין usually means a husband or father annulling a vow (הפרה), but here it refers to a חכם releasing a vow (התרה), which is what רבן גמליאל did.

phrases.english: And we learned many things at that time.
We learned that a quarter-log of Italian wine intoxicates,
and we learned that a drunk person should not issue a ruling,
and we learned that the road makes wine wear off,
and we learned that one does not annul vows

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָכוּב וְלֹא מְהַלֵּךְ וְלֹא עוֹמֵד,
phrases.english: not while riding, nor walking, nor standing,
but only while sitting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws halachic lessons from the story told in steps 13-14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רביעית of Italian wine intoxicates; a שיכור may not rule; travel dispels wine; vows are released only while sitting.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says it took three מילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier rule that walking one מיל removes the effect of wine, since in the ברייתא it took three מילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches three מילין! (So how can we say one מיל is enough?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the story to attack the earlier statement on the דף that a journey of one מיל makes wine wear off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רמי בר אבא said that walking a מיל or sleeping a little removes the effect of wine. If one מיל were enough, רבן גמליאל should have released the vow after one מיל. The ברייתא shows him waiting for three, which seems to contradict that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, at any rate

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches three mil!
phrases.notes: Out of the whole long story, the גמרא zooms in on the one detail that matters for its challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story to the halachic question about how fast wine wears off, using the three-מיל detail from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement (רמי בר אבא) that a journey of one מיל dispels the effect of wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one מיל were enough, רבן גמליאל would not have needed three מילין before releasing the vow.

steps.title: Italian wine is stronger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that Italian wine is especially intoxicating, so it needs more travel to wear off. Ordinary wine still wears off after one מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Italian wine is different, because it makes a person more drunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by saying the story involved an unusually strong wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one-מיל rule stays in place for regular wine. Italian wine is an exception because it is stronger, so its effect takes longer to fade. That is why רבן גמליאל needed three מילין.
steps.whatToRemember: Normally a מיל of travel sobers someone who drank a רביעית, but strong Italian wine needs more, which is why רבן גמליאל waited three מילין.

phrases.english: Italian wine is different
because it intoxicates more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (an exception for unusually strong wine)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that wine always needs three מילין to wear off, contradicting the one-מיל rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one-מיל rule applies to ordinary wine. Italian wine is stronger and needs a longer journey.

steps.title: Travel should make a person who drank a lot even drunker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: travel sobers a person only after a רביעית. After more than a רביעית, travel tires him and sleep makes him drunker. Italian wine is strong, so it should count like more than a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב נחמן say in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This rule (that travel sobers you up) applies only to someone who drank a רביעית. If he drank more than a רביעית, the travel tires him out even more, and sleep makes him even drunker!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 17. If Italian wine is extra strong, travel should have made רבן גמליאל worse, not better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said Italian wine is so strong that it needs three מילין to wear off. That means a רביעית of it acts like a larger amount of ordinary wine. But רב נחמן taught that with a larger amount, travel does not help at all. It only exhausts the person, and then sleep makes him drunker. So how did the trip help?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (introduces a contradicting source)
They only taught [this rule] in the case of

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman say
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
They taught this only where he drank a quarter-log,
but if he drank more than a quarter-log,
all the more so the journey exhausts him
phrases.notes: The travel tires him out instead of clearing his head.

phrases.english: and sleep makes him drunker!
phrases.notes: When he finally rests, a short sleep makes the drunkenness worse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 17 that Italian wine needs more travel.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that three מילין of travel sobered up רבן גמליאל after strong Italian wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Strong wine counts like more than a רביעית. According to רב נחמן, after more than a רביעית travel makes a person worse, not sober.

steps.title: Riding is different from walking
steps.stepSummary: Riding on an animal is not exhausting like walking. So the travel cleared the wine without tiring רבן גמליאל out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Riding is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 18. רבן גמליאל was riding, not walking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's warning is about walking, which tires a person out. A rider is not worn out by the trip, so the travel only helps the wine wear off. This lets three מילין of riding work even after strong Italian wine.

phrases.english: Riding is different.
phrases.notes: A rider does not get exhausted the way a walker does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any travel after strong wine exhausts a person and makes him drunker.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן's rule is about walking. Riding does not tire a person, so it helps the wine wear off.

steps.title: The same answer also resolves the question on רמי בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: Now that riding is different, the earlier question on רמי בר אבא, who said one מיל is enough, also goes away. Riding wears off wine more slowly than walking, so three מילין were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this idea, there is also no difficulty with רמי בר אבא: riding is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from Step 16 and gives it a new answer using the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 asked why the trip took three מילין when רמי בר אבא said one מיל is enough. Step 17 answered that Italian wine is strong. Now there is a simpler answer: רמי בר אבא's one מיל refers to walking. Riding is less effort, so the wine wears off more slowly, and three מילין are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this [idea]

steps.confusionAlert: The same fact, riding, is used in two different ways. In Step 19 it means riding does NOT exhaust you, so travel helps. Here it means riding sobers you more SLOWLY than walking, so you need more distance. Both come from the fact that riding takes less effort.
steps.whatToRemember: Riding is different from walking. Riding does not exhaust a person, but it also sobers him up more slowly. This explains both why the trip helped רבן גמליאל and why it took three מילין.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,

phrases.aramaic: לְרָמִי בַּר אַבָּא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: according to Rami bar Abba it is also not difficult:
riding is different.
phrases.notes: His one מיל refers to walking. Riding takes longer to sober a person up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 19 to give a new answer to the question of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a new distinction to an earlier question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three מילין could only be explained by the strength of Italian wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: רמי בר אבא's one מיל refers to walking. Riding needs more distance.

steps.title: Why did רבן גמליאל get off his donkey to release the vow?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן said vows may be released while walking, standing, or riding. So why did רבן גמליאל get off his donkey and sit?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But didn't רב נחמן say: One may release vows whether walking, standing, or riding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges another detail of the story: רבן גמליאל getting off his donkey and sitting before releasing the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 learned from the story that vows are released only while sitting. But רב נחמן clearly allows releasing vows while walking, standing, or riding. The story and רב נחמן seem to contradict each other.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word מפירין refers to a חכם releasing a vow (התרת נדרים). It does not refer to the הפרה of a husband or father.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Nachman say:
One may release vows

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מְהַלֵּךְ בֵּין עוֹמֵד וּבֵין רָכוּב!
phrases.english: whether walking, standing, or riding!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wine issue to the vow-release detail of the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lesson from Step 15 that vows may only be released while sitting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן allows releasing a vow in any position, so there was no need for רבן גמליאל to get off his donkey and sit.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים about how a vow is released
steps.stepSummary: This is a disagreement between תנאים. One opinion holds that a vow may be opened just through regret, which is easy to do in any position. רבן גמליאל followed the view that requires sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. For there is an opinion that says: we open [the release of a vow] through regret.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן and the story each follow a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the view that a vow can be opened through חרטה alone, the חכם only needs to see that the person regrets the vow. This is a simple check that can be done while walking, standing, or riding, and רב נחמן follows this view. רבן גמליאל held that releasing a vow needs a more careful process, done while sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
We open [an opening to release a vow]

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how a vow is released depends on how much the process requires. Simple regret can be checked anywhere, while a more formal process calls for sitting.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im.
For there is one who says:
we open [the release] through regret.
phrases.notes: No special reason is needed. It is enough that the person regrets the vow, which can be checked in any position.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two positions to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is one rule for everyone about the position needed to release a vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן follows the view that regret alone opens the vow, so any position works. רבן גמליאל required sitting.

steps.title: The other opinion: regret alone cannot open a vow
steps.stepSummary: This completes the תנאים dispute from Step 22. There is an opinion that a vow cannot be opened by regret alone, and רבן גמליאל followed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is someone who says: we do not open a vow through regret.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the second side of the dispute between תנאים. This is the side רבן גמליאל followed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If regret is not enough, the חכם has to find a real 'opening' (פתח), a reason to undo the vow. Finding one takes careful thought, so it is done sitting down. That explains why רבן גמליאל got off his donkey and sat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Open' a vow, meaning find a way to release it
Regret about having made the vow
There is someone who says (introduces another opinion)

phrases.english: And there is one who says:
one may not open [a vow] by means of regret.
phrases.notes: A specific 'opening' is required, which needs focus. That is why one sits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided dispute that Step 22 used as its answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Releasing a vow is always easy, so position should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to this opinion, a real opening is needed. That requires careful thought, so one must sit.

steps.title: The actual opening רבן גמליאל used
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבן גמליאל released the vow using a פסוק from משלי. This shows he used a real opening, not just regret.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What opening did רבן גמליאל give that man? The verse 'There is one who utters like the piercings of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.' This means anyone who makes a vow deserves to be pierced by a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support that רבן גמליאל used a real 'opening'. He quoted a פסוק teaching that vowing is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening works like this: 'Had you known that vowing is this serious, would you have vowed?' The man says no, and the חכם can release the vow. Because רבן גמליאל needed this kind of opening, he followed the view that requires sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: One who utters, here meaning one who makes a vow
The tongue of the wise heals (a חכם releasing the vow)
Opened for him, meaning gave him a basis for releasing the vow

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל sat because he held that a vow needs a real opening, not just regret. His opening was the פסוק 'יש בוטה כמדקרות חרב'.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי פָּתַח לֵיהּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא:
phrases.english: With what did Rabban Gamliel open [the vow] for that man?
"There is one who utters like the piercings of a sword,
phrases.notes: משלי 12:18

phrases.english: but the tongue of the wise heals":
Anyone who utters [a vow] deserves to be pierced with a sword,
but the tongue of the wise heals.
phrases.notes: A חכם's release undoes the vow from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 23 by showing that רבן גמליאל used a specific opening.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל held a vow needs a real opening, not just regret
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's report of the פסוק רבן גמליאל used as his opening

steps.title: Passing by food applied only in earlier generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule that one may not pass by food. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי limits it to earlier generations, before witchcraft became common.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: One may not pass by food. רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: This was taught only in earlier generations, when Jewish women were not involved in witchcraft. But in later generations, when Jewish women are involved in witchcraft, one may pass by food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to another lesson from the ברייתא about רבן גמליאל: do not pass by food lying on the road. It then limits that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule shows respect for food: you should pick it up. In later times, bread left on the road might have had a spell cast on it, so touching it could be dangerous. Avoiding danger outweighs showing respect for food.

keyTerms.meaning: Pass by (and leave the food lying there)
They only taught this in the case of (a limitation)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the idea of respect for food. It is an exception for times when the food might be dangerous.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: וְאֵין מַעֲבִירִין עַל הָאוֹכָלִין.
phrases.english: The Master said: And one may not pass by food.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
They taught this only in the earlier generations,
when Jewish women were not accustomed to witchcraft.
But in the later generations,
when Jewish women are accustomed to witchcraft, one may pass by [food].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וְאֵין מַעֲבִירִין עַל הָאוֹכָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of vows and takes up a different lesson from the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on passing by food applied in earlier generations. In later generations, when witchcraft is common, one may pass it by.

steps.title: Whole loaves may be passed by, pieces may not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא narrows the leniency. One may pass by whole loaves, but not pieces of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Whole loaves, one may pass by. Pieces, one may not pass by.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא spells out exactly which food the later-generation leniency covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whole loaves might have been set down on purpose for sorcery, so one may leave them. Pieces of bread are assumed not to be used for sorcery, so the original rule stays: pick them up.

phrases.english: It was taught: whole [loaves], one may pass by;
pieces, one may not pass by.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the leniency from Step 25 to whole loaves only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whole loaves may be passed by. Pieces of bread may not.

steps.title: A verse suggests sorcery was done with pieces of bread
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי asks רב אשי: don't sorcerers use pieces too? A פסוק in יחזקאל mentions pieces of bread together with sorcery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said to רב אשי: And do they not do sorcery with pieces? But it is written: 'And you have profaned Me among My people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי challenges the ברייתא. He uses a פסוק to suggest that pieces of bread were also used in sorcery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes that only whole loaves carry a risk of sorcery. The פסוק, which describes false prophetesses, mentions 'pieces of bread'. That seems to show pieces were part of sorcery too, so they should also be allowed to be passed by.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַסִּי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said to Rav Ashi:
And do they not perform [sorcery] with pieces?
But isn't it written: "And you have profaned Me among My people
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 13:19, about false prophetesses

phrases.english: for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line the ברייתא in Step 26 drew between whole loaves and pieces.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that pieces of bread may not be passed by
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק connects pieces of bread to sorcery. So pieces should carry the same danger as whole loaves.

steps.title: The pieces were the sorcerers' payment
steps.stepSummary: The pieces of bread in the פסוק were payment the sorceresses received, not tools for their magic.
steps.simpleTranslation: They took them as their wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אסי by reading the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For pieces of bread' means 'in exchange for' pieces of bread, as payment. The פסוק does not show that pieces were used to cast spells. So the ברייתא stands: pieces carry no sorcery risk and should not be passed by.
steps.whatToRemember: One may not pass by food. In later generations one may pass by whole loaves, because of the fear of sorcery, but one must still pick up pieces of bread.

phrases.english: [It means] that they took them as their wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in Step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק shows that pieces of bread were used to perform sorcery.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pieces were payment for the sorcery, not tools of it. So the ברייתא's distinction holds.

steps.title: Introducing a teaching of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה through רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement. רב ששת is about to quote a teaching he received in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It tells us who is speaking, רב ששת, and whose teaching he is passing on, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The actual statement comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only gives the chain of who said what. רב ששת is an אמורא, and he is reporting a teaching from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a much earlier תנא. Do not look for a ruling here yet. The new content is in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of. It means he is quoting someone else's teaching

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only an introduction. It is not a complete statement. Wait for the next line to see what רבי אלעזר בן עזריה actually taught.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the side discussion about food and sorcery from steps 25–28. It starts a new statement, and the content of that statement follows on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only attributes a teaching that רב ששת reports in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the teaching itself follows in the next line.
